title: Opening the club to play Dixieland, August 1951
summary: Sid wanted to be his own boss and play the music he liked; the club became the third Dixieland room on Bourbon Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Mardi Gras Lounge, 333 Berlin Street. Okay, Sid, can you tell me first of all, when you first started to run the club, what it was that first made you want to bring a jazz band in, whatever that was?

Well, I had been a musician playing around the country and playing in New Orleans for many years. Roy Zimmerman, Monk Hazel, and Leon Prima. When it was an opportunity for me to go into a business for myself, I couldn't think of anything I'd like to do better than open a club and put in the kind of music that we liked to play and enjoyed playing. And we killed two birds with one stone, I'd be the boss. Actually, I couldn't get fired that way. And no one could dictate what type of music we wanted to play.
And at the time, there were just a couple of other clubs on the street.
There were Patek Lounge and Famous Door. So we became the third club for Dixieland Music in the city, presenting Dixieland Music nightly.
Can you remember when that was? This was 1951, August 51.
And we continued that policy for a number of years, which was a happy occasion. And we made a lot of friends and employed a lot of wonderful musicians, you know?
